claims.text: Competition between temperature-accelerated atomic diffusion and lattice-distortion energy barriers governs the stability of equiatomic multimetal nanoparticles.
Random, uniform elemental mixing produces intrinsically strong interatomic bonding.
Strong interatomic bonding can kinetically limit surface segregation.
Strong interatomic bonding can kinetically limit local compositional fluctuations.
When diffusion is limited by the proposed barriers, nanoparticles retain a single-phase solid solution across 473–1923 K.
If elevated diffusion rates overcome the proposed barriers, local elemental segregation occurs.
Local elemental segregation initiates secondary-phase formation.
Secondary-phase formation compromises the stability of the initial solid solution.
The initial material is a chemically homogeneous, single-phase nanoparticle solid solution containing five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios.
The nanoparticles will be heated systematically from 473 K to 1923 K while being monitored by in situ electron microscopy and spectroscopy.
Minimizing oxidation and contamination is necessary for the predicted behavior to apply.
Increasing temperature increases atomic mobility and diffusion.
Lattice distortion arising from random multielement bonding imposes barriers to diffusion.
Nanoparticles with stronger kinetically limiting interactions will retain chemical homogeneity and a stable solid-solution morphology.
Nanoparticles with faster diffusion and weaker interactions will exhibit compositional inhomogeneity before reaching 1923 K.
Nanoparticles with faster diffusion and weaker interactions will exhibit secondary-phase formation before reaching 1923 K.
Significant departures from equiatomic composition may alter the predicted stability behavior.
The precise temperatures at which diffusion overcomes the proposed barriers are uncertain.
Catalytic reactive species may introduce additional effects on stability.
An absence of correlation between diffusion kinetics and the onset of structural or compositional instability would falsify the proposed mechanism.
